ASSISTANT TURN 32 (1 messages, last privileged)
[last] Yes. This is now a clean two-PR stack in Agent VM.

```text
Agent VM master
    │
    ▼
PR1 — Tool VM configured CLI
    │
    ▼
PR2 — Hermes execute_code → Tool Portal
```

PR1 — same configured-CLI call, different execution location

```text
tool_portal_call
  └─ configured CLI invocation
      ├─ same argv input
      ├─ same allowed command paths
      ├─ same flag restrictions
      ├─ same denied patterns
      ├─ same stdin validation
      ├─ same approval classification
      ├─ same timeout/output limits
      │
      └─ execution location differs
          ├─ existing: credentialed ephemeral VM
          └─ new: leased Tool VM through strict SSH
```

The caller should not care which VM executes it. Configuration selects the execution target.

PR1 decision:

```text
configured_cli.executionTarget
  ├─ controller_host
  ├─ ephemeral_managed_vm
  └─ tool_vm
```

Conceptually, the Tool VM call should look exactly like the existing ephemeral-VM configured-CLI call. Agent VM reuses the existing validation and policy behavior, then dispatches the validated argv through the existing Tool VM runner.

PR2 — programmatic Tool Portal composition

```text
Hermes execute_code
  │
  │ Python calls hermes_tools
  ▼
tool_portal_list / search / describe / call
  │
  │ RPC back to parent Hermes
  ▼
Agent VM Tool Portal
  │
  ├─ MCP provider
  ├─ controller host
  ├─ credentialed ephemeral VM
  └─ leased Tool VM
  │
  ▼
result returned to Python
  │
  ▼
Python filters, joins, loops, branches, and makes another call
```

The Python code must not know or care where a capability executes. It calls Tool Portal by namespace and name; Tool Portal selects the configured backend.

That enables compositions such as:

```text
Perplexity MCP
  → process result in Python
  → Firecrawl MCP
  → process result
  → Parallel CLI in Tool VM
  → compare and reduce
  → return one result to Hermes
```

PR stack record:

```text
PR1
  Agent VM configured CLI gains Tool VM execution target.

PR2
  Based on PR1.
  Separate worktree and stacked branch.
  Hermes execute_code gains Tool Portal list/search/describe/call helpers.
  Calls retain current agent identity, policy, backend routing, and limits.
```

One policy point remains: I am assuming Tool Portal calls made from `execute_code` keep normal approval behavior—including pausing for Hermes approval when required—instead of limiting programmatic calls to `withoutApproval`. Is that correct?
